questions.question: Which language should the frontend use?
questions.rationale: The existing Next.js starter is configured for TypeScript.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Adds static typing to the existing TypeScript starter.

questions.question: Which frontend framework should the dashboard use?
questions.rationale: The repository already uses Next.js 16.4.3 and React 19.3.0.

options.label: Next.js
options.description: Continue with the repository's existing React framework.

questions.question: Are there any additional frontend features or preferences to include?
questions.answer: Clean finance dashboard with income entry, basic filters, monthly totals, category breakdown, and trend.
questions.rationale: These are part of the already-approved baseline.
questions.recommendedChoice: Clean finance dashboard with income entry, basic filters, monthly totals, category breakdown, and trend.

questions.question: Which language should the backend use?
questions.rationale: The existing Next.js starter is configured for TypeScript.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Use the same typed language as the existing Next.js application.

questions.question: Which backend framework should provide the income-entry and dashboard data APIs?
questions.rationale: The repository is a Next.js starter; keeping the API in the same app avoids introducing an unrequested separate service.

options.label: Next.js Route Handlers
options.description: Keep the API in the existing Next.js application.

questions.question: Are there any additional backend features or preferences to include?
questions.answer: Manual income-entry CRUD and basic filters, with monthly totals, category breakdown, and trend; use Prisma with PostgreSQL.
questions.rationale: These are part of the already-approved baseline and existing local development setup.
questions.recommendedChoice: Manual income-entry CRUD and basic filters, with monthly totals, category breakdown, and trend; use Prisma with PostgreSQL.

questions.question: Which single currency should the income tracker use for entry amounts and totals?
questions.rationale: The user explicitly approved GBP for the implementation.

questions.question: What exact fields should each manual income entry contain? For example: date, amount, category, source or payer, and an optional note.
questions.answer: Date, amount, category, source or payer, and an optional note.
questions.rationale: Manual entry and category reporting are approved, but the exact entry fields remain unspecified.
questions.recommendedChoice: Date, amount, category, source or payer, and an optional note.

questions.question: Which data stores should this project use?
questions.rationale: PostgreSQL is part of the existing local Docker Compose setup and Prisma is approved; no file storage is needed in the stated baseline.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: The application does not need persistent data storage.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Relational database for income entries and derived reporting.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Object storage for files and media.

questions.question: Will users sign in to use application features?
questions.rationale: Single-user/no sign-in is part of the already-approved baseline.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users sign in to access application features.

options.label: No
options.description: The application is single-user with no sign-in.
